info.name: Pyas API v2
info.description:
The [Pyas](https://pyas.io) API v2: Google Calendar, Microsoft Outlook, Zoom and virtual calendars through one API. Generated from the API's OpenAPI document, and tested against the API before each release.

## Start in your sandbox

1. Fork this collection.
2. In the collection's **Variables**, paste a test key (`pyas_sk_test_...`, from your app's API keys in the Pyas dashboard) into `apiKey`.
3. Send any request.

A test key reaches your app's sandbox only: people with calendars and a week of events, and simulated Google, Outlook and Zoom accounts. Nothing touches a real calendar. Pyas never publishes a key, so the variable is empty until you fill it, and it is a secret variable.

The examples name the sandbox's data instead of its IDs: `{{account.avery}}` is Avery Brooks's account, `{{event.avery.design}}` the Design Review on her calendar. Before your first request, the collection's pre-request script reads `GET /v2/sandbox` and stores your sandbox's IDs under those names. `{{in.1d.14:00}}` is tomorrow at 14:00 UTC, and `{{in.-7d}}` a week ago, worked out before each request.

Every request sends your key once, from the collection, as the `x-api-key` header. Every request that creates, changes or deletes something gets a new `Idempotency-Key`, so a request resent by mistake never makes the change twice.

## What is here

- **A folder per resource,** as in the [API reference](https://developer.pyas.io/reference): every operation, with its description and an example you can send as it is. PyasConnect's requests from the browser are left out, as in the reference's Try it.
- **Scenarios,** 10 common jobs step by step. Run a scenario's folder with the Collection Runner: each step keeps what the next one needs, such as `{{slot.startsAt}}`. The first request of the Scenarios folder resets your sandbox.
- **Tests on every request:** the status, the response's `success` and `traceId`, and for an error its code and a link to its documentation. Run the collection as a smoke test of your own sandbox.

Some examples change the sandbox (one deletes an account, another the sandbox inbox). `POST /v2/sandbox/reset`, in the Sandbox folder, puts it back as new.

## Webhooks

Postman can't receive webhooks. To see them while you develop, run `npx @pyas/cli webhooks listen --forward http://localhost:3000/webhooks` (the Pyas CLI): it relays your sandbox's events to your own handler, signed as in production. `POST /v2/webhooks/{webhookId}/test` sends a sample delivery to an endpoint, and the sandbox inbox (`{{webhook.inbox}}`) records every event your sandbox sends.

## More

- Docs: https://developer.pyas.io
- Errors: every error links to its page, such as https://developer.pyas.io/errors/RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND
- The Node.js SDK: `npm install @pyas/sdk`

request.description:
Returns the status of each account. `overall.status` is `healthy`, `attention` or `broken`, and `overall` includes the reason and the fix. The response also shows which features are available, and includes a message for the account's owner when they need to take action. `meta.needsAttention` is the number of accounts in the response whose `overall.status` is not `healthy`.

With `accountIds` or `subjectId`, returns those accounts. Without them, returns every account of the app in the order they were added, one page at a time. To find every account that needs fixing, send `overall=attention,broken`. A page can include fewer than `limit` accounts even when `meta.nextCursor` is set, so keep requesting pages until `meta.nextCursor` is `null`. `check` works only with `accountIds` or `subjectId`.

**In the sandbox:** Lists every account in the app that needs action. In a new sandbox, every account works, so the list is empty. To check particular accounts instead, send `accountIds` or `subjectId`.

request.description:
Deletes an account from your app and sends a `connection.deleted` webhook.

For a Google, Outlook or Zoom account, Pyas deletes the credentials it stores for the account and stops watching it for changes. The user's calendars at the provider are not changed, and the user can connect the account again later. With a live key, the account no longer counts toward your plan.

For every account, the metadata you stored on its events and calendars is deleted too. In the sandbox, resetting the sandbox restores deleted accounts.

**In the sandbox:** This example deletes the simulated Google account in the sandbox. Virtual accounts are deleted the same way. Resetting the sandbox with `POST /v2/sandbox/reset` restores deleted sandbox accounts.

Exchanges the code for tokens, saves the account and returns it. This is the second step of connecting an account from your server without PyasConnect, and it replaces v1's `POST /{provider}/connect`. Send the `code` that the provider returned. If the same person connects an account that is already connected, Pyas reconnects it and the account keeps its `accountId`.

header.description: A unique key that makes the request safe to retry. A retry with the same key returns the original response and does not make the change twice. Keys are kept for 24 hours. Made for each request by the collection's pre-request script.

request.description:
Creates a session for connecting a calendar account. This is the first step of connecting with PyasConnect. Call it from your server. With a live key, the user signs in to Google, Microsoft or Zoom and a real account is connected. With a test key, the user sees a Pyas sandbox page instead of the provider's sign-in, and a simulated account is connected in your sandbox, so you can build and test the whole flow before going live. In popup mode, pass the `token` to your page. In redirect mode, set a `returnUrl` and send the user to `url`. A session is valid for 10 minutes and connects one account.

**In the sandbox:** Pass the `token` to PyasConnect on your page. With a test key, PyasConnect opens a Pyas sandbox page instead of Google or Microsoft, and connects a simulated account in your sandbox. For redirect mode, add a `returnUrl` on one of your app's allowed origins. To reconnect a broken account, send its `accountId` instead of `providers` and `subjectId`.

`POST /v2/connect/sessions`

Operation ID: `connect.sessions.create`
